## Commands, caps and source postconditions

Use one isolated feature-empty CLI check followed serially by two `cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test <installer_target> --no-run --message-format=json` operations. No --features host/ui, default/full graph, --lib, actual binary/help/install/test/--list, provider or native app execution. The same original Cargo JSON must uniquely identify each actual integration harness and matched CLI; build-finished must be exactly one success per compile. Compiling fixture bodies does not run their installer/guardian/Python branches.

Proposed source caps are600/900/900 seconds under one absolute2400-second workload deadline, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2. These reuse finite CLI-only caps, not measured cold-fit or cache warmth. Retain bounded Rust/native-dependency setup with original streams/exits (existing rustup600 and CLI apt1200 recipe); cache save/artifact steps need finite step/job deadlines, e.g. original90-minute hosted job and explicit10-minute save cap. Root must freeze exact final caps; none grants extra work after a failure or finite positive teardown. Unknown physical settlement retains external C/HOLD. All setup, checkout, build, validation, save/compression, upload and post actions count within ONE externally held C; A/B remain counted occupied2 and no second cold job runs.

Before saving, validate the produced target against the **same existing read-only CLI presence shape**, without calling the full restore gate with invented restore metadata. No root-library presence or harness compilation is called a five-parent pass, Cargo freshness proof or successful future restore.

## Exact save and visibility contract

Save ONLY after the three original commands, original writers/children and final source/context/custody checks succeed. Use pinned `actions/cache/save@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830`, the existing ordered three paths and the exact existing key expression in bindings.json. The prefix is `held1922-Linux-X64-rust193-bca4125b50134707a8afdb92ce04572c6ca6b3d3e43d177c5c679cecbc89c91b-` and the suffix is the actual40-hex producer control head; do not append a feature/manifest/run identifier or use the old ac4 key. Key lock hash is SHA256 of the one binary SHA256 lock digest, matching GitHub hashFiles. The source manifest/375 tree and actual compiler identity are separate receipt bindings; they are not extra key fields.

[GitHub's cache reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#restrictions-for-accessing-a-cache) scopes PR-created entries to the merge ref. Consequently this design targets only future runs of the same PR1921/ref, not main or another PR. Requested cache paths and compression/version compatibility also matter. A saved entry may later be unavailable; identical key text alone does not prove restore visibility or payload contents. No cache listing, lookup or restore was performed here.

The [pinned save action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/cache/0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830/save/action.yml) declares no output receipt. Its [save implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/cache/0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830/src/saveImpl.ts) can catch errors, warn and exit0. Therefore neither action outcome success nor a green workflow establishes publication. Sole original RAW must isolate the official vendor save step's explicit `Cache saved with key:` confirmation for the exact intended key, preserve any warning/cancellation, and bind original run/attempt/ref/control/product/version/path evidence. Do not scrape arbitrary build output or invent a cache-id output.
